hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test at Cape Canaveral
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Launch Complex 36 in Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night at 9pm ET. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad seconds after the test began, with the orange glow visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. The blast sent shockwaves across Florida's space coast, causing homes to shake in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all company employees were safe and uninjured. He described it as "a very rough day" on social media, noting that while the root cause remains unknown, the company is already investigating. "It's worth it," Bezos tweeted about rebuilding and returning to flight operations.

The explosion carries significant implications for NASA's lunar program. Just two days before the test, NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three uncrewed missions this year to begin constructing a 20 billion dollar moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use for these lunar lander missions, including those that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface as part of the Artemis program.

NASA administrator Jared Isaacman stated that a full evaluation of the program's timeline would be conducted following the incident. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he wrote on social media. NASA said it will work with Blue Origin to support a thorough investigation and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

The explosion marks another setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading to a temporary FAA grounding. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight operations.

Blue Origin described the incident as "an anomaly." The company and SpaceX both operate facilities at Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions with NASA. Under the Artemis program, Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System will compete to determine which system will carry astronauts from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface during planned missions in 2027 and 2028.

Elon Musk commented briefly on the incident on social media, stating "Most unfortunate" and noting that "Rockets are hard."

The FAA did not immediately respond regarding whether the explosion would trigger a new investigation. Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or hazardous materials, though flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the explosion.

cards.headline: Trump delays final decision on Iran ceasefire extension
cards.teaser: The president convened a Situation Room meeting but has not yet determined whether to approve a tentative framework reached between U.S. and Iranian officials.
cards.body:
President Trump convened a meeting with advisers to determine whether to extend a ceasefire agreement with Iran, but refrained from announcing a final decision. U.S. and Iranian officials have reached agreement on a framework for a deal that would require Trump's approval to proceed.

The proposed arrangement would extend the current ceasefire between the two nations. Trump's meeting followed confirmation from officials that both countries had agreed on the deal's framework.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop as U.S. and Iran Near Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as investors responded to signs that the United States and Iran were moving closer to a deal to extend a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil markets declined following indications that the United States and Iran were approaching an agreement on extending a cease-fire. The tentative signs of a potential pact prompted shifts in energy trading.

Stock markets showed mixed reactions as investors evaluated the diplomatic developments. The movement in oil prices reflected market expectations about how a U.S.-Iran agreement might affect global energy supplies and geopolitical stability in oil-producing regions.

cards.headline: European Union Prepares to Release Billions to Hungary After Orban's Defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros previously withheld as Hungary moves to enact anti-corruption and rule of law policies.
cards.body:
The European Union will release more than 16 billion euros to Hungary that had been frozen under Viktor Orbán's rule. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the decision as evidence of "winds of change" following the election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar last month.

The financial breakthrough reflects Hungary's progress on anti-corruption and rule of law reforms. The policy shift extends beyond economics—Hungarian police have announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest, reversing last year's government-ordered ban on the event.

cards.headline: Airlines warn of chaos as Mullin considers pulling customs officers from Newark
cards.teaser: The administration is weighing a plan to restrict international flights at airports in jurisdictions it considers sanctuary cities.
cards.body:
Airlines and business groups have warned of travel disruptions if the U.S. moves forward with plans to pull customs officers from Newark airport. The proposal, being considered by official Mullin, would target airports in sanctuary jurisdictions as part of immigration enforcement efforts.

The plan to punish sanctuary cities by affecting their airports has drawn opposition from the airline industry and faces significant resistance. Business groups argue that restricting international flights would create chaos for travelers and harm commerce.

cards.headline: Death toll reaches 9 in Longview paper mill disaster
cards.body:
Nine people have been confirmed dead following a chemical tank rupture at a paper mill in Longview, Washington. Recovery crews discovered the remains of a ninth victim on Friday, leaving two workers still unaccounted for.

The disaster occurred at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility on Tuesday morning when an industrial tank ruptured and released white liquor, a highly destructive chemical mixture used in kraft paper production. The tank held approximately 600,000 gallons of a liquid made mostly of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide. About 25,000 gallons remain in the damaged tank and continue leaking slowly.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson stated at a news conference that officials were "bracing ourselves for this being the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history." The initial incident killed one person immediately and injured nine others, including a firefighter who responded to the scene. Seven workers remain hospitalized.

Recovery operations began Wednesday after a delay caused by safety concerns about the structural integrity of the damaged tank. The Longview fire department said the operation transitioned from rescue to recovery, with no hope of finding additional survivors. Matt Amos with the fire department described the process as "slow, methodical and deliberate," noting that crews would ensure responder safety while treating victims "with the greatest dignity, care and respect as possible."

The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board arrived Wednesday to launch a federal investigation into the fatal implosion. The cause remains unknown. Safety complaints were filed against Nippon Dynawave in March and May, though the state's labor and industries department said both were unrelated to the current situation. The company has faced three separate health and safety violations since 2021, resulting in a $3,400 fine.

When the tank ruptured, the chemical spilled into a drainage ditch and contaminated the Columbia River, where dead carp were found. The Washington state department of ecology and EPA are overseeing environmental cleanup operations. Officials urged the public to avoid ditches and dikes during water testing but said there were no issues with air quality or drinking water in the city of about 40,000 residents.

Brian Wood, representing Nippon Dynawave, said the company was focused on victims and would "cooperate to the maximum extent" with investigators. The sprawling Longview plant employs about 1,000 people and produces material for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons.

Among the victims were two brothers who worked together, a trivia champion, and an electrician known for helping farmer neighbors cut hay. Community members gathered at a vigil Tuesday night, with residents expressing frustration about unanswered questions regarding the incident.

cards.headline: Bus collision in Virginia kills 5, injures 34
cards.teaser: A bus struck multiple cars, leaving five people dead and dozens injured, according to state police.
cards.body:
Five people died and 34 were injured when a bus collided with cars in Virginia, state police reported. The crash involved multiple vehicles and resulted in one of the state's deadliest traffic accidents in recent months.

State police are investigating the circumstances that led to the collision. The severity of the crash and the number of casualties required a multi-agency emergency response to treat the injured and clear the scene.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Romanian Apartment Building, Injuring Civilians
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Romania near the Ukrainian border, injuring civilians in the first such incident affecting noncombatants in the NATO member country, according to Romanian officials.

Romania shares a border with Ukraine and has faced growing threats from drones used in the nearby conflict. NATO condemned what it called Russia's recklessness in an episode that sharply escalated tensions with Moscow.

A Russian official warned European nations to prepare for more drone incidents following the Romania strike. The official suggested that Europe's peaceful period had ended, though specific details about future threats were not provided.

The drone impact marks a significant escalation in the spillover effects of the conflict in Ukraine. Previous drone incursions into Romanian airspace had occurred, but this represents the first time civilians were harmed on Romanian soil.

NATO member states issued statements condemning Russia for the incident. The security alliance's response highlighted concerns about the violation of a member nation's airspace and the danger posed to civilian populations.

Romanian officials confirmed the drone originated from Russian operations but did not immediately detail the extent of injuries or damage to the apartment building. The location near the Ukrainian border places the building in an area that has seen increased military activity as the conflict continues.

The incident raises questions about air defense capabilities and the protection of civilian areas in countries neighboring active conflict zones. Romania, as a NATO member, benefits from the alliance's collective defense provisions, which state that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

Russian authorities have not issued an official response to the incident or the warnings from their official about future drone activity in European airspace. The strike comes amid ongoing tensions between Russia and NATO countries over the conflict in Ukraine and broader security concerns in Eastern Europe.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Decision on Iran Cease-Fire Proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers at the White House but did not announce a determination on a possible cease-fire extension.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers for two hours at the White House to discuss a potential cease-fire extension with Iran. The meeting followed Trump's earlier social media indication that he was prepared to announce a decision on the matter.

U.S. and Iranian officials had previously reached agreement on a framework for a deal, though final terms continue to be negotiated. No agreement was announced following the White House meeting.

cards.headline: Iranian Hard-Liners Push Back Against Potential U.S. Deal
cards.teaser: A small but vocal faction in Iran has used rallies and state media to try to undermine ongoing negotiations with the United States.
cards.body:
A political struggle is taking place in Iran as hard-liners work to undermine potential negotiations with the United States. The faction has employed rallies, state media coverage, and public and private statements to oppose the talks.

Though the hard-line group represents a small faction within Iranian politics, they have maintained a prominent voice in the debate over U.S. engagement. Their efforts continue as negotiators work toward finalizing an agreement.

cards.headline: European Union Prepares to Release Billions to Hungary After Orban's Defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros previously withheld as Hungary moves to enact anti-corruption and rule of law policies.
cards.body:
The European Union will release more than 16 billion euros to Hungary that had been frozen under Viktor Orbán's rule. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the decision as evidence of "winds of change" following the election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar last month.

The financial breakthrough reflects Hungary's progress on anti-corruption and rule of law reforms. The policy shift extends beyond economics—Hungarian police have announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest, reversing last year's government-ordered ban on the event.

cards.headline: Ghana Parliament Passes Bill Criminalizing LGBTQ Activities
cards.teaser: Same-sex acts will be punishable by jail terms under new legislation targeting those identifying as gay, lesbian or transgender.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has approved legislation that criminalizes same-sex acts and the promotion of LGBTQ activities. Under the new bill, individuals identifying as gay, lesbian, or transgender face potential jail sentences.

The measure now requires the president's signature to become law. Lawmakers framed the bill as addressing what they view as the promotion of LGBTQ activities within the country.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding 14 Suicides
cards.teaser: A Canadian man admitted to selling toxic chemicals online to people who used them to kill themselves.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law appeared in an Ontario courtroom and pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide. Prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges as part of the agreement. Law had operated an online operation selling lethal chemicals with instructions to people across multiple countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand.

The guilty plea means Law avoided a murder trial. Sentencing is scheduled for September. Families of victims in Britain have called for additional charges, citing 79 deaths in the UK linked to Law's activities.

cards.headline: Trump Administration's Boat Strikes Fail to Reduce Cocaine Flow
cards.teaser: Despite rising casualties off the South American coast, cocaine remains as accessible in many U.S. regions as before the strikes began.
cards.body:
Military strikes on boats off the South American coast ordered by the Trump administration have not curbed the flow of cocaine into the United States, according to researchers. The operations have resulted in a rising body count but have failed to reduce drug availability.

Experts say cocaine is as easy to obtain in many parts of the United States as it was before the strikes began. The findings suggest the enforcement strategy has not achieved its stated goal of disrupting drug trafficking routes.

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Bondi testifies in Epstein files probe
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi told lawmakers that redaction errors were made during the release of Epstein-related documents and shifted responsibility to Todd Blanche.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before lawmakers investigating how the Justice Department handled files related to Jeffrey Epstein. She acknowledged that redaction errors occurred when the documents were released but distanced herself from responsibility for the mistakes.

During the hearing, Bondi shifted blame to Todd Blanche, drawing Democratic attention to his role in the matter. She declined to answer questions about President Trump as part of the investigation. The testimony occurred about a month after Trump removed Bondi from her position as the nation's top prosecutor.

cards.headline: Bus collision in Virginia kills 5, injures 34
cards.teaser: A bus struck multiple cars, leaving five people dead and dozens injured, according to state police.
cards.body:
Five people died and 34 were injured when a bus collided with cars in Virginia, state police reported. The crash involved multiple vehicles and resulted in one of the state's deadliest traffic accidents in recent months.

State police are investigating the circumstances that led to the collision. The severity of the crash and the number of casualties required a multi-agency emergency response to treat the injured and clear the scene.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Kennedy Center closure and name change
cards.teaser: A federal judge ordered the removal of President Trump's name from the memorial and blocked plans to close the venue.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that President Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center and blocked a planned two-year closure for renovations. In a 94-page ruling, the judge stated it was "crystal clear" that the performing arts center was named for President John F. Kennedy and must remain open to continue its programming.

Trump responded to the decision, saying he has no interest in the Kennedy Center. The ruling halts the administration's plan to rename and extensively renovate the Washington venue.

cards.headline: Airlines warn of chaos as Mullin considers pulling customs officers from Newark
cards.teaser: The administration is weighing a plan to restrict international flights at airports in jurisdictions it considers sanctuary cities.
cards.body:
Airlines and business groups have warned of travel disruptions if the U.S. moves forward with plans to pull customs officers from Newark airport. The proposal, being considered by official Mullin, would target airports in sanctuary jurisdictions as part of immigration enforcement efforts.

The plan to punish sanctuary cities by affecting their airports has drawn opposition from the airline industry and faces significant resistance. Business groups argue that restricting international flights would create chaos for travelers and harm commerce.

cards.headline: Trump postpones call with Taiwan president
cards.teaser: A planned conversation between President Trump and Taiwan's president has been put on hold.
cards.body:
President Trump's scheduled call with the Taiwanese president has been delayed. The postponement comes amid broader discussions about U.S. arms sales to Taiwan, which remain a point of tension with China.

Reports indicate Beijing has pushed the Trump administration to slow the pace of arms transfers to Taiwan. A delayed arms deal is dominated by air defense systems, according to sources familiar with the arrangement.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes Repeal of Climate Disclosure Rule
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a regulation requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed repealing a rule requiring companies to disclose their greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related risks. The regulation was implemented during the Biden administration.

The proposed repeal would eliminate reporting requirements intended to give investors information about companies' environmental impact and climate vulnerabilities. This move reverses the previous administration's approach to corporate climate disclosures.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop as U.S. and Iran Near Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as investors responded to signs that the United States and Iran were moving closer to a deal to extend a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil markets declined following indications that the United States and Iran were approaching an agreement on extending a cease-fire. The tentative signs of a potential pact prompted shifts in energy trading.

Stock markets showed mixed reactions as investors evaluated the diplomatic developments. The movement in oil prices reflected market expectations about how a U.S.-Iran agreement might affect global energy supplies and geopolitical stability in oil-producing regions.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Hit Record Highs on Technology Gains
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes closed at record levels with Dell leading technology sector advances, marking the ninth consecutive weekly gain for the S&P 500.
cards.body:
Major U.S. stock indexes closed at record levels, with technology stocks leading the advance. Dell's strong performance was particularly influential in driving gains across the tech sector and contributing to the broader market rally.

The S&P 500 achieved its ninth consecutive week of gains, capping a robust May for the broader market. The Nasdaq climbed 8 percent for the month as technology companies continued to fuel market momentum.

cards.headline: Universal Music Rejects Bill Ackman's Takeover Offer
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group turned down a takeover bid from billionaire Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, saying the offer undervalued the company.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group has rejected a takeover proposal from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management, valued at approximately $64-65 billion. The music company determined that the offer fundamentally undervalued the business.

Ackman, who already holds a stake in Universal Music Group, saw his bid to acquire full control of the music giant declined. Universal's rejection represents a significant obstacle to Ackman's plans to take over the company, which controls valuable recording rights and catalogs from major artists.

cards.headline: Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Supplement Sold Through Major Retailers
cards.teaser: Health officials connected a salmonella outbreak to moringa capsules sold through Amazon, Walmart, Target, and other retailers, prompting recalls.
cards.body:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention identified a multistate salmonella outbreak connected to moringa supplement capsules. People in both eastern and western Washington were among those affected by the contaminated products.

The supplements were distributed through major retailers including Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart, and Target. The Food and Drug Administration issued recalls for the affected products due to salmonella contamination.

cards.headline: Train Fire at Penn Station Injures Five, Disrupts Commuter Service
cards.teaser: A maintenance train fire near Penn Station injured five people and caused delays for Amtrak, Long Island Rail Road, and New Jersey Transit during evening rush hour.
cards.body:
A fire involving an Amtrak maintenance train near Penn Station injured five people and disrupted rail service for multiple commuter lines. The incident occurred during rush hour, affecting Amtrak, Long Island Rail Road, and New Jersey Transit passengers.

Services faced delays of up to 60 minutes as crews responded to the fire. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority described tunnel repairs at Penn Station as a chronic problem following the latest incident.

hero.headline: Indiana quarterback Brendan Sorsby bet on Hoosiers football at least 40 times
hero.body:
Indiana quarterback Brendan Sorsby placed at least 40 bets involving Indiana football while playing for the Hoosiers, according to court documents filed Friday. Sorsby wagered approximately $90,000 over four years using sportsbook accounts registered to a family member and friends.

The court documents revealed the extent of Sorsby's gambling activities during his tenure as quarterback for Indiana. The use of accounts belonging to others suggests an attempt to conceal the betting activity from authorities and athletic compliance officials.

The revelation carries serious implications for both Sorsby and the Indiana football program. NCAA rules strictly prohibit athletes from betting on their own sports, and penalties can include suspension or permanent ineligibility. The use of third-party accounts to place bets may compound potential violations.

The four-year timeline indicates the betting occurred throughout Sorsby's college career at Indiana. The $90,000 figure represents a substantial sum for a college athlete, raising questions about the source of funds and the scope of the gambling operation.

Friday's court filing brought the matter into public view, though the documents did not specify whether Sorsby bet for or against Indiana in the games or what charges may be pending. The filing also did not identify which family member or friends provided their accounts for the betting activity.

The case adds to a growing list of gambling scandals in college athletics. Several athletes across different sports have faced investigations and suspensions in recent years as sports betting has expanded across the United States. The NCAA has increased enforcement efforts as legal sports betting has become more accessible.

Indiana University has not released a statement regarding Sorsby's status with the team. The Big Ten Conference and NCAA will likely conduct their own investigations into the matter based on the information revealed in the court documents.

cards.headline: Djokovic loses to Fonseca in French Open third round
cards.teaser: Novak Djokovic's pursuit of a record 25th Grand Slam title ended with a third-round loss to Joao Fonseca at the French Open.
cards.body:
Brazilian teenager João Fonseca defeated Novak Djokovic in a five-set epic at Roland Garros, winning 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5. Djokovic had dominated the opening sets on Court Philippe-Chatrier, but the 19-year-old mounted a dramatic comeback to eliminate the 24-time Grand Slam champion.

The match stretched over four grueling hours as Djokovic's physical condition deteriorated. The 39-year-old struggled to maintain his advantage as Fonseca's youth and energy prevailed, denying Djokovic his pursuit of a record 25th major title. Fonseca advanced to the fourth round with the victory.

cards.headline: Giants teammates Carter and Dart express solidarity after Trump event dispute
cards.teaser: Giants teammates Abdul Carter and Jaxson Dart said they remain united after a disagreement over the quarterback's participation in an event for President Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Giants linebacker Abdul Carter and quarterback Jaxson Dart expressed solidarity Friday following a disagreement over Dart's involvement in an event for President Donald Trump. The teammates made public statements emphasizing their continued unity and support for one another.

The two players addressed the situation to move past the dispute that had drawn attention within the organization.

cards.headline: Thunder forward Jalen Williams out for Game 7 against Spurs
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City Thunder forward Jalen Williams will miss Saturday's Game 7 against the San Antonio Spurs due to injuries that have limited him all season.
cards.body:
Thunder wing Jalen Williams will miss Saturday's Game 7 against the Spurs due to injury. The absence affects Oklahoma City's roster for the elimination game in the Western Conference finals.

The series heads back to Oklahoma City after San Antonio's dominant 118-91 victory in Game 6. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 28 points and 10 rebounds. The winner of Saturday's Game 7 will advance to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

cards.headline: Giants receiver Gunner Olszewski suffers suspected torn Achilles
cards.teaser: Giants wide receiver Gunner Olszewski went down with a noncontact injury during OTAs that the team fears is a torn Achilles tendon.
cards.body:
Giants wide receiver Gunner Olszewski suffered a noncontact injury during Friday's organized team activities. The team fears the injury is a torn Achilles tendon, according to ESPN sources.

Olszewski was forced to leave the field following the incident. The severity of the injury remains to be determined pending medical evaluation.

cards.headline: 76ers hire Cavaliers general manager Mike Gansey as president of basketball operations
cards.teaser: Cleveland Cavaliers general manager Mike Gansey finalized a multiyear deal to become president of basketball operations for the Philadelphia 76ers.
cards.body:
Original Card (Unchanged)

Mike Gansey finalized a multiyear contract to become the new president of basketball operations for the Philadelphia 76ers, according to his agent Bret Just of WME Basketball. Gansey leaves his position as general manager of the Cleveland Cavaliers for the role.

The 76ers hired Gansey to oversee their basketball operations department in a multiyear agreement. Gansey's agent confirmed the deal on Friday, marking a significant move in NBA front office personnel.

---

Note: The additional source material provided (BBC News articles about Pam Bondi and energy bills) is unrelated to the 76ers/Gansey story, so the original card text is returned unchanged per your instructions.

cards.headline: White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami exits with hamstring tightness
cards.teaser: Chicago White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami left Friday's game against Detroit in the third inning with right hamstring tightness.
cards.body:
White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami left Friday's game against the Detroit Tigers in the third inning due to right hamstring tightness.

The early exit removes one of the team's key offensive players from the lineup.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the film editor who won an Academy Award for her work on Star Wars and helped shape several influential films of the 1970s, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer. Lucas was the former wife of Star Wars director George Lucas.

Her editing work extended beyond the original Star Wars film. She also edited American Graffiti, which earned her critical acclaim as a storyteller and technician in an era when few women held prominent roles in film editing.

Lucas received recognition as a trailblazer in the film industry. Her contributions to Star Wars helped define the pacing and narrative structure of one of the most successful film franchises in cinema history. The original Star Wars film, released in 1977, became a cultural phenomenon that transformed the entertainment industry.

Her family described her as a brilliant storyteller whose influence on filmmaking extended far beyond her Oscar win. She worked during a transformative period in Hollywood, when new approaches to editing and visual storytelling were reshaping how audiences experienced cinema.

Lucas's work on Star Wars involved assembling footage into the final theatrical cut that millions of viewers would see. Film editors play a crucial role in determining the rhythm, tension, and emotional impact of a movie, choices that can make or break a film's success.

Beyond her technical skills, Lucas was remembered for her creative vision and ability to see how disparate pieces of footage could come together to tell a compelling story. Her editing decisions on Star Wars helped create the film's distinctive pace and energy.

She lived in Rancho Mirage in her later years. Her death marks the loss of a key figure from the team that created one of the most enduring franchises in entertainment history, and a pioneer for women working in film editing during the 1970s.

cards.headline: Over Half of Freedom 250 Concert Performers Cancel Over Politics and Threats
cards.teaser: More than half of the artists scheduled to perform at Trump-backed Freedom 250 concerts have withdrawn from the events.
cards.body:
Artists including Martina McBride and Morris Day have canceled their appearances at the Freedom 250 concert series, part of events planned for America's 250th anniversary. The concerts are linked to former President Trump and are separate from the official America250 celebration.

The cancellations follow political controversy and threats directed at performers. The wave of withdrawals has left organizers of the Great American State Fair concerts scrambling to fill performance slots. The Freedom 250 series represents one of two separate approaches to celebrating the nation's semiquincentennial, with competing visions for how to mark the milestone.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Concerts Due to Health Issues
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling all remaining tour dates this year to focus on his health.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli apologized to fans who purchased tickets to his shows in a statement posted to social media on Friday. The performer, known for his decades-long career and continued touring into his nineties, said he made the decision to focus on his health.

Valli expressed disappointment about canceling the concerts but indicated the decision was necessary. He did not provide specific details about his health condition. The cancellations affect all scheduled performances for the remainder of 2026.

cards.headline: Erika Kirk Denies Dating Rumors Months After Husband Charlie Kirk's Death
cards.teaser: The widow of Charlie Kirk rejected claims that she has a new boyfriend less than a year after her husband's assassination.
cards.body:
Erika Kirk responded to rumors circulating online that she has started a new relationship following the death of her husband Charlie Kirk. She dismissed the speculation and said her late husband's love will last her a lifetime.

Charlie Kirk was assassinated earlier this year. Erika Kirk criticized those spreading the rumors, telling them to "go touch grass." The rumors emerged on social media platforms, prompting her direct public response. Multiple outlets reported on her denial of the claims.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Film Earns Over $10 Million in Previews Ahead of Wide Release
cards.teaser: The horror film from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons has already generated significant box office revenue before its nationwide opening.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the directorial debut from 20-year-old Kane Parsons, grossed more than $10 million during preview screenings. The A24 film features Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Mark Duplass, Finn Bennett, Avan Jogia, and Lukita Maxwell and is now playing in theaters nationwide.

The film adapts a popular YouTube series that introduced the Backrooms concept to audiences online. Parsons transformed the horror phenomenon into a theatrical feature, with the strong preview earnings indicating substantial audience interest in the property.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Uncapped Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman appeared with entertainment industry figures to call for unlimited production incentives ahead of Tuesday's election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman called on candidates for governor to back uncapped tax incentives for film and television production in California. She made the appeal outside Radford Studios on Friday, joined by entertainment figures including Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon who support her mayoral campaign.

Raman argued that California must ensure Hollywood remains a center of production. The event took place in the final days before Tuesday's gubernatorial election. Tax incentives for film and TV production have been a recurring policy debate in California as productions increasingly film in other states and countries.

cards.headline: 13 Reasons Why Stars Reunite at Filipino Forces Event in Hollywood
cards.teaser: Ross Butler and Timothy Granaderos appeared together at the annual gathering of influential Filipinos in entertainment and other industries.
cards.body:
The actors attended the fourth annual Filipino Forces event, a dinner bringing together Filipinos across fashion, entertainment, and technology. Butler and Granaderos both starred in the Netflix series 13 Reasons Why.
\

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., ruled that President Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center, dealing a setback to the administration's planned renovation of the performing arts venue.

The order signed by a district judge requires the removal of Trump's name from the building and surrounding signage within two weeks. The ruling also halted the scheduled closure of the facility, which was set to shut down later this year for renovations.

The judge wrote in a 94-page ruling that it was crystal clear that the arts complex was named for the late President John F. Kennedy. The decision concluded that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its statutory authority by unilaterally making changes to the facility's name.

The ruling prevents the center from winding down its programming and closing for two years of planned renovations, at least temporarily. The Kennedy Center had been scheduled to close later this year to begin the work.

The case centers on whether the board had legal authority to rename or rebrand the facility. The judge determined that the board's actions violated the bounds of its statutory powers regarding the venue, which was established as a memorial to President Kennedy.

President Trump has promoted renovations to the Kennedy Center as part of his administration's efforts to update federal buildings and cultural institutions in Washington. The ruling represents a legal challenge to those plans and to the administration's approach to managing the historic venue.

The two-week deadline for removing Trump's name from the building and signage creates an immediate compliance requirement for the Kennedy Center's administration. The halted closure means programming at the performing arts venue will continue for now.

cards.headline: Pentagon awards Dell $9.7 billion contract amid Trump stock ownership
cards.teaser: The Defense Department signed a five-year agreement with Dell for Microsoft software and cloud services after the president purchased stock in the company.
cards.body:
The Pentagon awarded Dell a $9.7 billion contract for Microsoft software and cloud services. The five-year agreement aims to consolidate the Department of Defense's technology services.

The contract has drawn scrutiny due to President Trump's financial stake in Dell. Trump purchased significant amounts of the company's stock and publicly promoted its products before the deal was finalized, raising questions about potential conflicts of interest.

cards.headline: Judge allows Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit to proceed
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to reopen the case after intervenors said a settlement creating an anti-weaponization fund tainted the proceedings.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the IRS seeking $10 billion. The decision came after parties who intervened in the case argued that a previously agreed settlement had compromised its integrity.

Trump and the Department of Justice had planned to voluntarily dismiss the suit in exchange for establishing an "anti-weaponization" fund. The judge sided with the intervenors, allowing the case to proceed for further scrutiny of Trump's claims against the tax agency.

cards.headline: New Jersey detention facility becomes test for DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: Protesters have been arrested outside Delaney Hall while detainees reportedly participate in a hunger strike over conditions.
cards.body:
A private immigration detention center in New Jersey has emerged as the first major test for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. The 1,000-bed Delaney Hall Facility in Newark has become a flashpoint over the Trump administration's immigration policies, with reports of protests and a hunger strike over living conditions and medical care.

State officials announced that New Jersey state police will take over policing functions from federal immigration officers outside the facility. Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced plans to establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators, as federal agents have increased their presence at the site.

cards.headline: Trump endorses challenger to Rep. Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: The president backed Lieutenant Governor Pam Evette over the sitting congresswoman seeking the governor's office.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lieutenant Governor Pam Evette over Representative Nancy Mace in the South Carolina governor's race. Trump called Evette an "America First Patriot" in a post on Truth Social, describing her as a good friend, fighter, and winner.

Mace, a Republican congresswoman, is running for the governor's office but will not receive the president's support in the primary contest.

cards.headline: Democrat leads Republican in Texas Senate race polling
cards.teaser: State Representative James Talarico held a three-point advantage over Attorney General Ken Paxton in a post-runoff poll.
cards.body:
State Representative James Talarico led Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton by three percentage points in a poll of likely general election voters. The survey from Texas Public Opinion Research showed Talarico with 47 percent support compared to 44 percent for Paxton.

The poll was conducted after the runoff election and measures voter preferences heading into the general election for the Senate seat. Talarico is the Democratic candidate while Paxton represents the Republican Party in the race.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary endorses $250 bill featuring Trump
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent backed a proposed currency to commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial during an interview at the Reagan Library.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed a proposed $250 bill featuring President Trump to commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial. Speaking at a White House news conference, Bessent said the Treasury has already begun preparing for the possibility of the new currency.

The proposal would require changing federal law, which currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency. Trump allies in Congress are working to make an exception, while Democrats have vowed to block the move.
